key_facts: On May 16, 2026, Plaintiff submitted two AT&T applications: R-107776 Retail Sales Consultant at Stockton Pacific and R-106742 Bilingual Spanish Retail Sales Consultant at Lodi. Both advanced through interviews. LTI then provided an ACTFL Telephone OPIc Spanish test expiring May 25 and stated that the rating would go to AT&T Taleo; the record still lacks the score, audio, threshold, receipt time, and decision notes. On May 28 at 10:13 a.m., Workday officially offered Plaintiff R-106742. The two-page offer identifies the position as Retail Sales Consultant reporting to Orville R. Bell at 2439 W. Kettleman Lane, $24.95/hour paid biweekly, $13,700 annual target variable compensation prorated for part-time hours, and a tentative June 15 start. It lists acceptance, hiring documents, work authorization, applicable export/rehire checks, absence of restrictive agreements, and satisfactory standardized background checks as contingencies; it does not list Spanish proficiency, at-will status, arbitration, weekly hours, or an unrestricted withdrawal right. Workday issued onboarding tasks at 10:15–10:17, and First Advantage sent a screening task at 10:19. At 12:23, Patterson texted that “the manager” no longer wanted to proceed because Plaintiff did not pass Spanish. The sequence proves an offer and abrupt rescission but not Workday acceptance, completed screening, report transmission, registry use, reliance loss, or discriminatory motive.
procedural_status: Verified complaint review draft generated for proposed September 8, 2026 execution; deliberately unsigned and unfiled. The uploaded two-page offer has been incorporated. Remaining pre-execution gates: (1) confirm exact acceptance method/time; (2) confirm which onboarding and First Advantage tasks Plaintiff completed; (3) identify each concrete act of reliance and alternative job/opportunity; (4) confirm no pre-adverse report or rights summary arrived through any email/portal; (5) verify factual allegations under penalty of perjury; and (6) verify current California agents for service. Discovery targets remain the AT&T Workday audit, R-106742/R-107776 disposition history, LTI score/transmission, Patterson/Bell communications, and the individual First Advantage order under client account 132156. No CRD charge or right-to-sue is recorded.
damages: The offer confirms $24.95/hour, biweekly pay, a $13,700 annual variable-compensation target prorated for part-time hours, and a tentative June 15, 2026 start. It does not state weekly hours. The record still lacks acceptance, reliance loss, mitigation period, and expected duration. Statutory remedies are contingent: Penal Code § 290.46(j)(4)(A) permits actual/treble relief with a $250 floor, fees, exemplary damages, or a civil penalty up to $25,000; ICRAA § 1786.50 permits actual damages or $10,000, whichever is greater, plus specified relief; FCRA remedies depend on negligent or willful violation. Portfolio valuation remains $0 until acceptance/reliance or report use is confirmed.
risk: High-risk review draft, not filing-ready. The offer materially strengthens specificity and the anomaly: it uses the non-bilingual title Retail Sales Consultant and omits Spanish passage from its listed contingencies after the test window closed. It still does not prove acceptance, reliance, or report use. The § 290.46/FCRA/ICRAA counts may be dismissed if no report was transmitted before 12:23; contract and estoppel may fail without acceptance/reliance; fraud lacks internal knowledge/intent facts; and UCL needs lost money/property and an equitable remedy. FEHA/Fair Chance counts remain omitted absent exhaustion. AT&T Mobility Services LLC and First Advantage Background Services Corp. remain probable, not offer-confirmed, entities.
